newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shekel unchanged against dollar.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shekel unchanged against dollar.

text.p: The Israeli shekel's representative rate was fixed unchanged against the dollar on Wednesday after the Bank of Israel intervened in the market on a relatively large scale, dealers said.
"The shekel closed unchanged today after the Bank of Israel intervened in trading, buying dollars on a high scale to support the basket," said a dealer at Israel Discount Bank.
Dealers estimated that the central bank bought more than $200 million to support the foreign exchange rate.
The central bank has been intervening regularly in the market to defend the currency basket, which has been trading at the bottom end of its band for two months.
"The business sector continues to take foreign currency-linked loans knowing that the shekel will remain at the bottom of the trading band," the dealer said.

The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.3570 shekels, unchanged from Tuesday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, was fixed at 3.6625 shekels against 3.6617 on Tuesday.
On the crosses, the shekel traded against the yen at 2.7425 shekels per 100 yen compared with 2.7136 on Tuesday, and against the mark at 2.0078 shekels after 2.0100 on Tuesday.
In the late afternoon, the dollar was trading at 3.3550 shekels.
